### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8fdf25a43707b03f2120941acd6acefbdd0b034a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5812b4d84a93fb7087a836a397f73afe5d87bd04` — the merge of head `bfa139bac599ca65a062b0486364ea25d7e57ce8` into base `8fdf25a43707b03f2120941acd6acefbdd0b034a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5812b4d84a93fb7087a836a397f73afe5d87bd04 && git checkout 5812b4d84a93fb7087a836a397f73afe5d87bd04
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8fdf25a43707b03f2120941acd6acefbdd0b034a bfa139bac599ca65a062b0486364ea25d7e57ce8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8fdf25a43707b03f2120941acd6acefbdd0b034a && git merge --no-ff bfa139bac599ca65a062b0486364ea25d7e57ce8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8fdf25a43707b03f2120941acd6acefbdd0b034a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67ff848e4cd5f759c80c2921854d18c66c8cb690`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (the extension walk's cycle call and its import only)

Inputs read: card #33153 (body, comments 6865769873, 6883476966, 6884342925), PR #33442 (body, 7 files, net diff against `main`, merge base `fc283d6d`), the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff read on `main`, not reviewed: `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts`, `packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts`, `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, `protocol-object-extension-item.ts`, `protocol-extension-redeclared-owner-field.ts`. None of these moved between the merge base and `main`.

Check-runs on the head when this record was written: 21 success, 10 skipped, 33 in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green among them: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate. Not concluded: Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Build Core, Type Check (workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates, UI), three Lint groups, Live E2E UI, Build & E2E UI. This record judges the contract and its implementing code; it does not answer for a check-run that had not concluded.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: `os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and the `object_extension` publish door refuse one more shape, a `formula` field an extension adds that sits on a cycle. A narrowing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are right, on the PR body and the changeset alike.
- Rule id and roster: no new rule id. The finding is `expression-invalid`, from `validateStackExpressions`, which already lists `object_extension` in its `runtimeTypes` on `main` (`authoring-rules.ts:851`, #33072). The door roster and its pins do not move: right.
- Public surface: `formulaCycleIssues` gains a second accepted `report` type and `extensionFormulaLoci` is new. Neither is exported from the package entry; the only importer at the head is `validate-expressions.ts`. "No exported type or signature changes" is right.
- ADR-0087: one semantic entry, id `object-extension-formula-cycle-refused`, file name `18.` plus the id, the changeset's marker names the same id. No D2 conversion, for a reason that holds (which read to cut is the author's fact). Right.
- First-party exposure: the two first-party extension files on `main` (`examples/app-showcase/src/data/extensions/account.extension.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts`) carry no `formula`. Nothing first-party is newly refused: right.
- Unchanged verdicts: the object walk's call is untouched (`formulaCycleIssues(objectName, fieldDefs, declaredNames)`), so a declared cycle keeps its finding and location. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor. The kind is `narrowed`, which takes at least minor on each package the diff moves; the diff moves lint (source) and spec (the registry entry). The runtime change is a test file and publishes nothing. The BREAKING banner, the Before / Now / Unchanged / Fix body and the ADR-0087 marker are present. Level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, no labels and no assignees: follows the order; no contract effect. Accepted.
- Deviation, no merge of `main`: the files this change reads and edits did not move between `fc283d6d` and `main` (checked for the two lint sources, `object-graph.ts`, `packages/formula/src` and the three door files). Accepted.
- Deviation, branch `claude/project-thread-j2hlfl` instead of `claude/issue-33153-*`: stated on the claim (6883476966). Accepted.
- File surface: all 7 files sit inside the claim's surface.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, the redeclared-name gap at the door, reported with `carrier: none` and not filed: not accepted as written. See finding 1; the mitigation the PR body gives for it does not cover every case, and the gap is wider than the one shape reported. Escalated to the seat as finding 1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts` against the code.**

- "reads its own value, itself or through the formulas it reads, the target's own formulas included": holds. The cycle pass runs over `fieldDefs`, the target as served (`typedObjects` at the target's position, declared fields and injected columns behind it), so a loop closing through a declared formula is found, and the added member is reported at the entry.
- "refused with the verdict and the sentence the object's own cycle gets": holds. Same function, same `formulaReadOrder` message, same `severity: 'error'`.
- "on each member the extension adds, located at the entry; a member the object declares keeps its location at the object": holds in the build. The object walk reports the names of its `fieldList`; the extension walk reports names NOT in `fieldEntries(base)`, the same authored body. The two sets are disjoint, so no member is named twice, and each walk iterates a member once.
- The example (`fields` as a name-keyed map) is read through `recordsOf`, which folds the key into `name`: it is refused as written.
- "a stored row is not re-judged until it is published again": holds. The door strips the written package's own stored extension from the target (`objectExtensionWriteFold`, `withoutExtensionsOf`), and a write bound to no package is refused before the gate (`objectExtensionItemRefusal`, step 1), so a republish that turns an existing extension field into a cycle member IS refused: the old field is not in `base`, so its name is in the loci.

**Attempts to break the implementing code.**

- Downstream readers: `formulaReadOrder` names strongly connected components only (Tarjan, plus a self-read). An extension formula that merely READS a member of the target's own cycle is not a member and is not refused. The door differential holds for it.
- Target's own cycle at the door: its members are in `base`, so they are outside the loci. Not charged. A sibling package's stored cycle on the same target is likewise in `base` and not charged.
- Two packages forming one cycle (build): `objectExtensionsByTarget` hands every kept entry for the target; each member is located at the entry that adds it, with the `packages[j].manifest.` prefix from `entry.path`. Holds.
- Two packages forming one cycle (door): A republishes `a__c` to read B's stored `b__c`, which reads `a__c`. `b__c` is in `base`, `a__c` is the written entry's: `a__c` is refused at the entry, `b__c` is not charged. Holds.
- Same name from two entries at different priorities: the list is sorted ascending by priority then carrier, the same order `objectsAsServed` folds in, so "located at the later one" is the definition served. Holds.
- A lower-priority entry's shadowed cyclic formula is not served and not reported. Consistent with "as served".
- Undeclared target: `fieldDefs` is the entries' own fields, `ownNames` is empty, every cyclic added formula is reported. Holds.
- `report instanceof Map` with the fallback location: a `Set` caller keeps the old location, a `Map` caller always has an entry for a name it `has`. No path yields a wrong location.

**Findings.**

1. **should-fix** — at the door, a cycle member whose NAME the door's target already serves is never refused, and the build disagrees. `ownNames` is `fieldEntries(base)`; in the build `base` is the authored object, but at the door it is the target as the registry serves it without the written package's extension, which includes every OTHER package's published extension fields. Two shapes get through the door:
   - (a) a package extending an object it owns and re-declaring one of its declared fields as a formula on a cycle. The PR body says such a re-declaration "is refused at the save door anyway (ADR-0146 D10)". That is true only for another package's object: `protocol-extension-redeclared-owner-field.ts` states "Not judged: an extension of an object its own package owns". For that case nothing refuses it at the door.
   - (b) a field the written entry adds under a name a sibling package's published extension also adds, at a higher priority, so the written definition is the one served. The owner does not declare it, so the entry does add it, and the contract's sentence "refused ... on each member the extension adds" is false for it at the door. The build refuses the same stack at the entry. The dev report does not name this shape.
   Both are rare, and both sit beside the card's Expected ("at both the build and the `object_extension` door"). A fix that keeps the differential: on the extension write, leave a name out of the report only when the served definition (`fieldDefs.get(name)`) is not one of the written entry's own field records. If the seat rules this out of the card instead, it needs a carrier (a follow-up card), and the PR body's D10 sentence corrected; `carrier: none` is not an answer.

2. **nit** — ties. A field two packages add at the same priority is dropped from the served body of a declared target (`objectsWithoutTiedFields`), so a cycle through it is not found, even when every tied definition is cyclic. The PR body states this and it follows the walk's existing treatment of a tie; the entry's `surface` and `acceptanceCriteria` state no exception, so "`os build` reports no finding" and "each formula reads a computed value" can part ways there. On an UNDECLARED target the tie is not dropped (`fieldDefs` takes the later entry's definition), so the call-site comment "(a tie left out)" is not true for that branch. No effect on any first-party or plausible stack. Accepted deviation, or a line in the changeset's Unchanged list.

3. **nit** — wording. `extensionFormulaLoci`'s jsdoc and the call-site comment call `declared` "a name the target declares itself"; at the door it is every name the target serves before the write. The words should say so once finding 1 is settled.

No must-fix. Finding 1 earns a delta review of its fix or of its carrier.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (the extension walk's cycle call, its comment and its import only)

Round 2. The round-1 record is comment 6884435411 on PR #33442, at head `67ff848e`. This record judges the new head on its own and then answers each round-1 finding.

Inputs read: card #33153 (body, comments 6865769873, 6883476966, 6884342925, 6885198948), PR #33442 (body, 7 files, comments, net diff against `main` with merge base `fc283d6d`, and the round's delta `67ff848e..7c2eeb88`), the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff read on `main`, not reviewed: `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` (`objectExtensionsByTarget`, `objectsAsServed`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts` (`objectExtensionWriteFold`). Between the merge base and `main` no file under `packages/lint` or `packages/formula/src` moved; `protocol-authoring-gate.ts` gained a locale option only.

Check-runs on the head: 72 runs, 60 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Concluded green: Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check and the four Type Check groups, every Lint group, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, Build & E2E UI.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: `os build`, `os validate`, `os lint` and the `object_extension` publish door refuse a `formula` field an extension adds that sits on a cycle. A narrowing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are right, on the PR body and the changeset.
- The round's delta narrows the door once more and leaves the build alone. The one code change is `base && !extensionWrite` in place of `base` when the left-out names are built. `extensionWrite` is `options.runtimeWriteType === 'object_extension'`, never true in a build, so every build verdict and location is what it was at `67ff848e`. Right.
- Rule id and roster: no new rule id, the finding stays `expression-invalid` from `validateStackExpressions`, already on the `object_extension` door. The roster and its pins do not move. Right.
- Public surface: `extensionFormulaLoci`'s third parameter is renamed `declared` to `left`. The function is not exported from the package entry and its one importer is `validate-expressions.ts`. "No exported type or signature changes" stays right.
- ADR-0087: one semantic entry, id `object-extension-formula-cycle-refused`, the changeset marker names the same id. Right.
- First-party exposure: unchanged from round 1 (no first-party extension adds a `formula`). Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, unchanged this round. The kind is `narrowed`; the diff moves lint (source) and spec (the registry entry); the runtime change is a test file. The BREAKING banner, the Before / Now / Unchanged / Fix body and the ADR-0087 marker are present. The level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` (6885198948): empty. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (6885198948): empty. The round-1 entry (`carrier: none`) is answered by the fix; see the round-1 status below.
- Deviation, the PR body written by the seat from the dev's draft: the body on the PR carries the round-1 content (the corrected D10 sentence, the new cases, ablation A3). Accepted.
- Deviation, no merge of `main` (now `b392ff7b`): the files this change edits and reads did not move in a way that touches it (checked above). Accepted.
- File surface: the same 7 files, all inside the claim's surface (6883476966).

### ④ Design judgment

**The key attack: no name is left out of the report on the door's write.**

- What `base` and `entries` are at the door: `objects` is the target as the registry serves it with the written package's own extension left out (`objectExtensionWriteFold`, `withoutExtensionsOf`), every other package's extension fields folded in as plain fields; `objectExtensions` is the written entry alone. `objectsAsServed` folds that entry over the target, "a later writer replacing the whole field", so `fieldDefs.get(name)` for a name the entry adds is the entry's own record. The report set is exactly the names of the written entry.
- The target's own stored cycle: its members are fields of `base` that the entry does not name, so they are not in the loci. Not charged. Pinned ("the differential").
- A sibling package's stored cycle: the same, its members sit in `base`. Not charged. Pinned this round.
- A formula that only reads a cycle member: `formulaReadOrder` names members of a strongly connected component only. The reader is in the loci but is not a member, so it gets no finding. Pinned this round, in the same case.
- An entry that re-declares a member of the target's own cycle: the whole field is replaced, so the member is a cycle member only if the entry's own expression puts it on one. A display-only re-declaration (no `expression`) takes the name off the cycle. The write is charged only for a cycle its own definition is on.
- Duplicate findings: at the door the object walk reads an empty list (`extensionWrite ? [] : objects`), so the extension walk is the only reporter and `formulaCycleIssues` iterates each member once. In the build the object walk reports `declaredNames` (the authored field list) and the extension walk leaves out `fieldEntries(base)` of the same authored body: disjoint, as at `67ff848e`. No member is named twice at either.
- Build verdict: unchanged by construction (① above). Shape (a) in the build is named once, at the object, as `main` already names it; the docs sentence now says the build and the door differ in location for that shape.

**`18.object-extension-formula-cycle-refused.ts` against the code.** `surface`, `replacement`, and the body of `reason` hold as judged in round 1. The two sentences added this round are judged in finding 1.

**Findings.**

1. **should-fix** — the door now reads the written entry's definition as the one served whatever a sibling's priority is, and three new sentences say otherwise. The door's `base` carries a sibling package's extension field as a plain field, with no priority, so the fold cannot see a tie or a higher sibling. Three consequences at this head:
   - (i) Tie. A sibling's published extension adds `s__c` at priority 200; the written entry adds `s__c` at priority 200 as a formula reading itself. The door refuses it (one entry, so `objectsAsServed` sees no tie). The build over both packages drops the tied name and reports nothing. The entry's `acceptanceCriteria` says such a cycle is one "which neither door judges", and its `reason` and the changeset's Unchanged list say the field "is not judged". That was true of the door at `67ff848e` (the name was left out) and stopped being true in the commit that wrote the sentence.
   - (ii) Outranked. The sibling adds `s__c` at priority 300, the written entry at 200 as a cyclic formula. The registry serves the sibling's definition; the build reports nothing (the shadowed definition is not served). The door refuses the write at the entry. So the door refuses a stack `os build` accepts. The call-site comment's "every name the entry adds is served from the entry's own record", the changeset's "the written definition is the one served" and the docs' "the written entry's fields are served over the target" are true of the gate's fold and not of the registry here. The new shape (b) pin sets the written entry at 300 over a sibling at 100, the winning case only.
   - (iii) The tie exception is also wider than the code on an undeclared target in the build: there the walk takes the later entry's definition of a shared name and judges it (the PR body says so; the entry and the changeset do not).
   All three are in the refusing direction, need two packages adding one field name to one object plus a formula cycle, and give the author a clear 422. No must-fix. But the `hits` file states a behaviour the door contradicts, so this is not a nit. Smallest fix: say in the entry (`reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), the changeset and the call-site comment that the tie exception is the build's on a declared target, and that the publish door judges the written entry's definition as served over the target whatever a sibling's priority; add a pin for (i) or (ii) at the door. Making the door agree with the build instead needs the sibling entries and their priorities in the door's snapshot, which is outside this diff and would be a follow-up card.

2. **nit** — PR body. 维护者速读 still says the two-minute run expects 12 cases (the file has 15 at this head), and "What changes" still writes `extensionFormulaLoci(target, entries, declared)`. Prose face; fixable without moving the head.

Observation, not charged to this PR: the same door snapshot gives a false negative when a higher-priority sibling's definition of a name the entry also adds closes a cycle through another field of the entry (the door folds the entry's definition over the sibling's and sees no cycle; the build reports the entry's member). That is a property of the #33072 snapshot, present at `67ff848e` and for every as-served check on that door. It belongs on the follow-up card named in finding 1, if one is filed.

**Round-1 findings (6884435411).**

- Finding 1 (should-fix, a cycle member under a name the target already serves never refused at the door): **resolved**. Shape (a), an own-package extension re-declaring a declared field as a cyclic formula, is refused at the door at the entry; shape (b) as written in round 1 (the written entry at the higher priority) is refused at the door at the entry and by the build at the later entry. Both are pinned at the real gate, and the dev's ablation of the guard turns exactly those two red. The door differential holds (above). The fix reaches further than shape (b) asked; that is finding 1 of this round.
- Finding 2 (nit, ties): **resolved as asked, with a residue**. The tie exception is stated in the entry's `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` and in the changeset's Unchanged list, and the call-site comment now describes the declared and the undeclared branch correctly. The stated exception is too wide for the door and for an undeclared target; carried in finding 1 of this round.
- Finding 3 (nit, `declared` wording): **resolved**. The parameter is `left`, and the jsdoc says what the build passes and what the door passes. The PR body's one stale spelling is finding 2 of this round.

No must-fix. Finding 1 earns a delta review of its fix or of its carrier.
